findings.title: Enable nix-command inside the workflow guard
findings.why_it_matters: The ci-workflow-docs-skip derivation fails before checking its matrix contract in a clean Linux build sandbox. The new subprocess uses the experimental nix eval command, but neither its arguments nor the derivation enable nix-command; the invoking developer or Actions runner's Nix configuration is not a declared sandbox input. Explicitly enabling the feature makes this pure expression evaluation independent of host configuration.
findings.validation_reason: The newly added tests/check-workflow-docs-skip.sh:277 invokes nix eval without enabling nix-command, and flake.nix:1608-1622 supplies no feature configuration; with Nix 2.34.9 and isolated configuration the same invocation fails with nix-command disabled, establishing the clean-config trigger although Linux sandbox incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Duplicate containers-auth probe creates parallel maintenance owners
findings.why_it_matters: Changes to the containers-auth lifecycle contract now require editing two byte-identical runtime probes, so a correction to permissions, preservation, or dry-run coverage can leave the other platform testing an older contract. The Linux and Darwin suites exercise distinct delivery boundaries and should remain independent, but their shared probe implementation need not be copied. Extracting the probe preserves both executions while giving the assertions one maintenance owner.
findings.validation_reason: Fresh comparison confirms that the new authEffects definitions at tests/podman-containers.nix:24-60 and tests/darwin-outputs.nix:105-141 are identical, so a lifecycle assertion correction requires parallel edits; both distinct platform callers execute the same probe and can retain their independent delivery coverage with a shared implementation.

evidence: tests/lib/agent-activation.py:65: `result = subprocess.run([bash, '-e', str(block)], env=current,`
tests/lib/agent-activation.py:56: `env.pop('DRY_RUN', None)`. Live runs are tested with DRY_RUN unset, the same as Home Manager's live runs, where DRY_RUN is only exported for dry runs.

home/h82/agents/agent-plugins.nix:203: `if [[ -v DRY_RUN ]]; then`. This is the -u-safe form; a refactor to `[ -n "$DRY_RUN" ]` would expand to empty under `bash -e`, take the live branch, and satisfy every call/args/Pi-link/refusal assertion plus the dry-run pass. Under HM's `set -u` the same line aborts activation.

home/h82/agents/agent-plugins.nix:257-259: 'linkGeneration sits behind these entries in the built activation script, so this position keeps a refusal from stranding installPackages but not from stranding linkGeneration' — so a -u abort here leaves home files unlinked.

Same diff, tests/podman-containers.nix authEffects: `subprocess.run(["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c", ...])`, and tests/vscodium.nix: `${pkgs.bash}/bin/bash -eu "$redirected"`. The shared harness is the weakest of the new execution harnesses.
Locally available pinned Home Manager source modules/home-environment.nix:860-863 sets -eu, pipefail and cd $HOME; reviewed harness line 65 passes only -e.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the block under the same shell options Home Manager's activation script uses: `subprocess.run([bash, '-euo', 'pipefail', str(block)], ...)`. Optionally set cwd=str(home) to match HM's `cd $HOME`. This is the same strictness the sibling harnesses in this diff already use: podman-containers/darwin-outputs authEffects use `-euo pipefail` and vscodium uses `-eu`.
findings.title: Activation harness runs without -u, passing blocks that abort under Home Manager
findings.why_it_matters: This harness is now the only runtime proof for the claude, codex-settings, gemini, tokscale and agent-plugins activation blocks. Home Manager runs activation under `set -eu` and `set -o pipefail`, but the harness runs each block with `bash -e` only. A block that reads an unset variable passes every harness assertion here, then aborts the real `home-manager switch` with an 'unbound variable' error. Per the module's own comment, a failure at that point strands linkGeneration, so the user's declared home files are never linked, while CI stays green.
findings.validation_reason: The newly introduced tests/lib/agent-activation.py:56-66 unsets DRY_RUN and executes blocks with bash -e only, whereas the available Home Manager modules/home-environment.nix:860-863 enables -eu and pipefail; replacing agent-plugins.nix:203 with an unguarded DRY_RUN expansion is therefore a reachable missed regression under the shared callers, although mutation incidence was not measured.
